biggest_catch: ProZ.com is a paid membership directory, not a work platform: translators are paid by direct clients they find there, so there is no platform pay rate and no platform payout schedule - plus full job-bidding access costs $180/year (Plus).
catches: No platform pay rate: each translator sets their own rates and negotiates with direct clients; ProZ.com publishes no worker pay.
No payout timing: clients pay translators directly - there is no platform payout schedule at all.
Meaningful visibility and job bidding require a paid Plus membership ($180/year); free registration is limited.
Income depends entirely on winning direct-client work through the directory; nothing is guaranteed.

c1.evidence: ProZ.com is a directory/membership marketplace; translators are paid by direct clients, not by the platform. No platform worker pay rate exists.

c2.evidence: No platform payout schedule exists; payments flow directly between clients and translators.

c3.evidence: Free registration exists, but full job-bidding features require paid Plus membership ($180/year) - pay-to-play for meaningful access.

eligibility: Freelance translator or interpreter; free registration possible; Plus membership ($180/year) needed for full job-bidding access.
maximize: If a route here ever qualified, the standard path would be: complete your profile fully (real name, native language, specializations - ProZ says over a third of directory searches exclude profiles without a native language entered), post competitive per-word rates, and actively bid on posted jobs rather than waiting for directory traffic. As it stands, ProZ.com is a lead source, not a paid platform.
notes: ProZ.com is a translator directory and job board. No platform-level worker pay or payout timing exists because payments occur directly between clients and translators.

Deliver work and invoice clients directly; payment terms are per client, not platform.
